body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).
- Contracted Enterprise accounts follow this matrix unless their order form names a different approver.
## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-estimates-for-sales-quotes-2026.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-09", "text": "title: Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes

No amount is promised before Finance's review |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.
## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.
| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|

Tell the customer the amount credited. |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "(continued) ## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit

This ticket consolidates fixes for the export pipeline, adds a deterministic rounding/aggregation strategy, and includes a backfill job to align historical exports for the last 90 days.

SELECT invoice_id, exported_total, SUM(line_amount) as computed_total, exported_total - SUM(line_amount) as diff_cents
FROM billing.invoice_lines l JOIN billing.exports e ON l.invoice_id = e.invoice_id
WHERE e.export_date >= '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY invoice_id, exported_total
HAVING ABS(exported_total - SUM(line_amount)) > 0.01;
  - -- Identify fractional credit patterns
SELECT invoice_id, COUNT(*) as credit_lines, SUM(line_amount) as credit_total
FROM billing.invoice_lines
WHERE credit_type = 'rate_limit_refund'
